recipes.name: Aloo Gobi
ingredients_raw: 2 medium baking potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 inch pieces

steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add cumin seeds; cook until turn golden brown and begin to pop, a few seconds; reduce heat to medium. Add onion; cook until lightly browned. Stir in serrano chiles and ginger paste; cook 1 minute. Season with coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper, garam masala, and paprika; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds.

Add potatoes and salt to the pot; cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes. Add cauliflower; cover and steam in its own juices until tender, about 20 minutes. Stir in lemon juice. Add remaining 1 tablespoon oil around edges of the pot. Increase heat to medium-high; cook until browned, 3 to 5 minutes, stirring gently to avoid mashing cauliflower.

raw_recipe.headline: Aloo Gobi
raw_recipe.description: Aloo gobi is a spiced cauliflower and potatoes Indian dish. The recipe steams then fries in oil, making it intentionally dry and somewhat crispy.

review.reviewBody: This was good and I will make this again. My house smelled like an Indian restaurant as I was making this. Chile peppers were omitted because I didn't have any. It will still moderately spicy. After 20 minutes, the cauliflower was still crunchy, so I ended up cooking it almost double the length stated in the recipe. I served it with whole wheat pitas and sour cream.

Quick, easy and delicious. I took the advice of others and nuked the cauliflower in the microwave for a couple of minutes first. I also added a splash of vegetable broth to the mixture as it was cooking to keep it from sticking and burning. Served over rice but you certainly don't need to. It's very filling even without the rice.

Outstanding, simple prep, easy to understand, easily accessible ingredients. Yep, it's hot. I didn't have any serranos on hand so I subbed some red pepper flakes AND used the full amount of cayenne. I also used organic extra virgin coconut oil for the saute which added a dimension of flavor. This one goes on heavy rotation when cauliflower is in season. I used an enamel coated cast iron Le Creuset pot to make this in. Potatoes having the starch that they do did stick to the bottom. I added small amounts of water during the process to deglaze the pot just a bit, which kind of sped up the cook time. For beginners I'd recommend a good quality non-stick pot with a lid.

Very yummy, I made it in the slow cooker for convenience, so I added a few fluid ounces of chicken broth and a handful of chopped grape tomatoes from the yard to save the pot from cracking, with a little chopped cilantro for garnish. I served it with plain yogurt and basmati rice made with half canned coconut milk and water. Husband at first complained about being meatless, but after one spoonful did a complete about face. Everyone loved it. I will make again. Thank you.

Amazing. I made this as directed except instead of doing it in a pot, I used my cast iron skillet and I used frozen cauliflower instead of fresh. The potatoes took about twice as long to cook, I added a bit of extra oil so they didn't stick and just stirred them occasionally. My cast iron skillet doesn't have a lid, so I just added a bit of water from time to time when cooking the cauliflower. It cooked beautifully and everything came out great. I will definitely make this again!

This was so delicious, and tasted very authentic! I made only a few minor changes. I didn't have any cumin seeds, so I just used ground cumin and added it in when the other spices went in; I'm sure using the seeds adds a bunch more flavor, so I'll need to get some for next time. I used two jalapenos instead of serrano peppers, and I added the spices by eye, but I'm pretty sure I added closer to a full teaspoon or maybe more for everything that called for just a half. I don't feel like the heat was too much; in fact, I will add more cayenne next time, but I'm used to eating spicy food.

As others have noted, adding coconut milk is not authentic, this is meant to be a dry dish, and it is perfect that way. I didn't have any issue with needing liquids, just make sure you add oil as needed. I cooked this in a cast iron pan, which I highly recommend doing. I will definitely be making this again, it's one of my new favorite dishes!

Edited to add: I've since gotten the cumin seeds and now use them every time I make this, which is usually every month now. I also use coriander seeds and put them in at the same time as the cumin instead of using the ground coriander, which I recommend trying!

It was great added frozen peas and fresh carrots.
Pre cook potatoes to help with the process.
I like my cauliflower firm so only put it in at the end for 5 mins.

My husband and I love spicy food so this was a great recipe for us! This is not for those who prefer mild dishes. Like Candice, I wanted the dish to be a little saucy so it could be served over rice. I used about 3/4 can of coconut milk. Also, I read the reviews which state that the cauliflower takes too long to cook. So while I was preparing the rest of the dish, I steamed the cauliflower in a separate pot. Then I added the steamed cauliflower to the dish to cut down on the cook time. Don't steam too much or the cauliflower will become mushy after cooking it with the rest of the dish.

I cooked the cauliflower for 5 minutes first in the microwave to soften a bit, then the 20 minute cooking time was about right. Also, I forgot to get a lemon, so I chopped a tomato to add some acidity at the end instead and fried for a couple minutes.

Pretty good recipe... although I did leave out the peppers (it was plenty spicy for me without!). I would cut the potatoes smaller, the cauliflower was done faster than the potatoes. I used a dutch oven to make this... probably would work better with a non-stick pan... all the spices were sticking to the bottom of the pot. I did de-glaze with some stock to pick these bits up!

I LOVE this recipe. However, it has taken me a few tries to figure out how to best orchestrate cooking all of the elements without scorching/turning things to mush/etc. The following works well for me: Cover the potatoes and cook them in some vegetable oil until they are pierceable but not fully done, stirring occasionally (takes around 10 minutes for me, but I usually double the recipe). Take them off the heat, THEN proceed with the recipe as written, adding the potatoes back in at the same time as the cauliflower. Also, I definitely recommend adding a bit of water to the spice mixture to form a paste--it prevents scorching so you don't end up with a nondescript "burnt Indian spice" flavor, but rather the fantastic combination of spices given in the recipe. Finally, I usually add a total of about a 1/2 cup of water while the whole dish is cooking, spread out over the full cooking time. You might get by without it, but it helps things to soften a little more quickly. The dish never comes out crunchy for me, but I honestly don't mind at all. Really a great (and super cheap, if you buy bulk spices!) recipe.
Needs garlic. And tomatoes. Otherwise amazing and very spicy.
Enjoyed the flavors, will need to try in a larger pot
I made this with no changes other than using jalapenos as we didn't have serrano peppers, and it was delicious!!!
Love it. Try roasting the cauliflower and potatoes instead though. Toss in a small amount of veg oil and bake for 22 minutes at 375- they wont be mushy that way.

Used the exact called for spices, minus the Serrano peppers, and the dish had very little flavor. After it was cooked I tasted it and it was very bland so I added more of each of the spices. Still very bland. No where near the authentic flavor I was looking for.

This is tasty and has a good spice to it. I only used one serrano chili and it was perfect. I made the mistake of putting the cauliflower in the pot the same time as the potatoes as I read a few reviews stating that the cauliflower took a long time to cook. This was not the case, and it got over-cooked. Just follow the directions as is.
I really like this, but it took me at least an hour and a half to cook it. And I added tomatoes to it and eliminated some of peppers and half the salt.
Delicious
Made it as per recipe and loved it! Definitely making again
